sources.entry: trafilatura - A tool for gathering text and metadata from the web, with built-in content filtering.

summary.one_liner: Trafilatura is a Python package and command-line tool for discovering web pages, downloading them, and extracting main text, metadata, and comments from raw HTML.
summary.what_it_does: It fetches live URLs and processes previously downloaded HTML files or parsed HTML trees, with parallel and polite download queues. It supports crawling via sitemaps (TXT, XML) and feeds (ATOM, JSON, RSS), plus URL filtering and deduplication. Its main-text extractor is rule-based, using jusText and readability-lxml as fallbacks, and it pulls metadata such as title, author, date, site name, categories and tags. Optional elements include comments, links, images, and tables, and optional add-ons cover language detection and speed optimizations. Output can be TXT, Markdown, CSV, JSON, HTML, XML, or XML-TEI. No database is required.
use_cases: extract article text from web pages
scrape metadata like title and author from pages
build text corpora for research or NLP
crawl websites via sitemaps and feeds
convert raw HTML to Markdown or JSON
how_to_run: Run in Python: from trafilatura import fetch_url, extract
extract(downloaded, output_format="json", with_metadata=True) to get text plus metadata
Use the command-line tool (see documentation for usage)
notable: Rule-based main-text extractor with jusText and readability-lxml fallbacks
Crawling support for sitemaps and web feeds with URL deduplication
Multiple output formats including XML-TEI and CSV
Works offline on saved HTML as well as live URLs
Reported benchmark results against other open-source extraction libraries
caveats: Versions prior to v1.8.0 are under GPLv3+ rather than Apache 2.0
Project depends on community support for continued maintenance, per the README
